title: Rose Revolution
summary: Nonviolent protests in Georgia began in early November 2003 after a disputed parliamentary election, with roses as the movement's symbol. Led by Mikheil Saakashvili, they forced President Eduard Shevardnadze to resign and brought new elections in January 2004, when Saakashvili was inaugurated.

uncertainty.note: Sources differ by a day on the start (3 vs 4 November 2003); end of protest period given as 25 November 2003 by Swarthmore.

where.modern_name: Tbilisi, Georgia (pin is the capital city centre, a proxy for the protests)

importance.justification: Early colour revolution that ended Shevardnadze's presidency and brought Saakashvili to power.
